prompt.query: Determine the mechanism and activation barrier of the Bergman cyclization of (Z)-hex-3-ene-1,5-diyne to p-benzyne (1,4-didehydrobenzene). Reactant SMILES: C#C/C=C\C#C; product SMILES: [c]1cc[c]cc1; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: gas phase, thermal. Within the allowed methods, model the system so that it approximates the real conditions stated above as closely as the level of theory permits. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [CH:1]#[C:2]/[CH:3]=[CH:4]\[C:5]#[CH:6]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. Use exactly this JSON shape (key names matter: nodes carry `id`, `role` (one of reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state) and `smiles` (a list of SMILES strings), and may optionally carry a `properties` object for declared quantities; edges carry `id`, `from`, `to`, `via`, `bond_changes` and optionally `barrier_kcal_mol`, `channel` and `favored`): {"nodes": [{"id": "RC", "role": "reactant", "smiles": ["..."]}, {"id": "TS1", "role": "transition_state", "smiles": []}, {"id": "P", "role": "product", "smiles": ["..."]}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "RC", "to": "P", "via": "TS1", "bond_changes": {"break": [[1, 2]], "form": [[1, 5]]}, "barrier_kcal_mol": 21.3}]}. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or state-change step carries two empty lists. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Declare the cyclization barrier in kcal/mol (transition state relative to the enediyne minimum) on the rate-determining step's edge as `barrier_kcal_mol` in mechanism_graph.json. Barriers are electronic energy differences (ΔE‡) in kcal/mol, without ZPE or thermal corrections, each relative to that step's own starting minimum. Additionally declare `reaction_energy_kcal_mol` in a `properties` object on the product node. If you conclude that the requested quantity cannot be computed to a trustworthy accuracy with the allowed methods, deliver mechanism_graph.json containing {"refusal": {"refused": true, "reason": "<the electronic-structure reason>"}} instead of a mechanism graph. The scorer reads that structured declaration, not prose; do not declare a number you cannot stand behind. Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.
